heard: A nearby planet completes its entire year in 18 hours. Discovered in 2004, 55 Kankri-e is a rocky super-Earth twice the size of our home world. It orbits its sun-like star so closely that the planet is tidally locked in a permanent death spiral. The star-facing dayside roasts at over 2,000 Kelvin, a temperature hot enough to melt iron. In 2012, one controversial hypothesis suggested this carbon-rich world might have an interior of solid diamond. But in 2024, the James Webb Space Telescope detected a thick, volatile atmosphere on this hellscape. This atmosphere is likely outgassed from and sustained by a bubbling ocean of liquid magma. That molten surface races around its host star in just 18 hours.
